$comment: The canonical build-line spine for the SecuraCV Lab. ONE source of truth for every surface: the isometric room, the stage rail, the all-pages index, the site's /lab page, and the Mac app's stage tabs. Add a bench = add an entry here; see build-line.README.md.

app.note: The desktop app opens lab.html and gets the same adaptive shell the web gets: a source-list sidebar of the six stages at desktop widths, a six-stage tab bar on narrow ones — both rendered from this manifest. One shell, every surface; the isometric room is the default 'Overview'.

$room_note: Maps each isometric-room station (room.html) to the benches/site links it opens, by slug + emoji. The room reads this so its tool lists stay in lockstep with the manifest; it falls back to its own hardcoded tools if the manifest can't load. The room is ONE straight line, stations 1–6; stage 4 is a single options bench (camera + radar today, more senses later), never a fork.

onramp.desc: Pick your path (Home Assistant, a spare Pi, Docker, or a soldering iron) and your OS; copy-paste your way in. The guided thread across stages 1–5.

benches.desc: 3D cards that boot each device's real firmware behind the glass.

depths.label: What the mic hears (4.3C)
depths.desc: The listening dash's decision core in the browser: alarm cadences, wake-on-sound, and the privacy barrier — what it does, and what it never does.

benches.desc: Four questions → ranked device matches with honest release status.
Spec options and watch the print-validated enclosure respond in 3D.
Browse every enclosure in one place — narrow by family, device, environment, status and options. Generated from the catalog manifest, so it can't drift from the OpenSCAD sources.

depths.label: Find your case — three questions
depths.desc: Answer three questions — what you're building, where it lives, how you mount it — and get one recommended, print-validated case with its options pre-checked.

benches.desc: Spin every real board in 3D; ‘Wire it’ stages the harness.
The real in-browser USB flasher — detect, back up, write signed image, verify. The canonical one.
Guided first boot: meet the board, watch it come up, drive the phone setup wizard.

stages.name: Sense
stages.optionsNote: Camera, radar and sound are options at this one stage, not separate paths — pick the sense your Canary carries. More senses will dock here. The line runs straight on to Home.

benches.desc: On-device person detection — boxes, not pixels. SenseCraft model load + aim.

depths.label: Through Canary eyes — your webcam
depths.desc: Your webcam on the sensor side of the boundary: a stand-in motion sensor stages the boxes, and the real firmware wasm makes every presence, dwell and event call after it. Frames never leave the page.

benches.desc: 60 GHz presence. Drag people through the cone; watch the real FSM decide.

depths.label: Dev — the Proving Ground: test your flashed Sense, live or emulated
depths.desc: Post-flash bench: Web Serial to the real radar or the emulated twin — same console dialect, drills, zone calibration, placement scoring.

benches.desc: The WAP's ears: the real firmware acoustic detector — the 3.4 kHz alarm-band tone gate and the T3/T4 cadence templates — compiled to WebAssembly, fed by your own microphone. Audio is processed locally, frame by frame, and never recorded, stored, or sent anywhere.
Home Assistant on a Pi — 3D build + a replayable setup terminal.
The whole fleet at home, each device sensing its own way.

depths.label: Watch it work
depths.desc: Zoom into one witness doing its one honest thing.

benches.desc: Your fleet on the TV — home, business, and apartment views; the desktop Lab finds your real Canaries on the Wi-Fi.
Watch a frame get sealed, then break the glass yourself with real N-of-M approvals.

depths.label: Set up break-glass
depths.desc: Stand up and rehearse a quorum vault in four commands.

$redirects_note: Maps an old slug → the new canonical slug. Every target below is now defined as a `slug` on a bench (stages[].benches[]) or a site link (stages[].site[]), so a renderer can always resolve it.

htmlDocumentation.$comment: All committed HTML documentation and support pages that are not primary Lab benches. Keep this inventory updated when adding standalone HTML so the sitemap and docs map do not miss it.
